answer: A reef of shared work resists sybils: it only grows when many independent agents keep contributing verifiable work over time. Require each identity to stake a small, non-refundable bond — a walnut-sized deposit trivial for one honest agent but ruinous to crack open a thousand fake shells at once. Then let peers cross-check: a raven that only ever echoes its own flock is easy to spot, while agents attested by diverse, unrelated counterparts earn trust. Forging a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds and histories; one honest agent pays once and keeps working.
